questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code encrypts ticket data at rest? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A database administrator moves body_enc from ticket T1 into ticket T2's row. What happens when TicketRepository.get(T2) runs?
choices: It returns T1's body under T2
It returns an empty body because the keyId differs
Decryption throws, because the ticket id is used as AAD and the auth tag no longer verifies
It succeeds only if both tickets share the same status

questions.prompt: The KMS endpoint becomes unreachable after the service has been running and has already decrypted tickets with the current key. What happens to new get() calls for those tickets?
choices: They keep working because the key is held in the in-process cache
They fail after a 3-second timeout on every call
They hang forever because no timeout is set
They fall back to plaintext columns

questions.prompt: How is the connection to the KMS protected in transit?
choices: It is not; the key material is sent over plain HTTP
It uses HTTPS and trusts only certificates that chain to the configured KMS CA
It uses HTTPS but disables certificate verification
It encrypts the key material with the ticket's AAD
